subject: Reseller withholding / pass-through invoice process for marketplace co-sell

Subject: Reseller withholding / pass-through invoice process for marketplace co-sell

Hi Sara / Luis,

Quick one as we kick off the CloudResell co-sell deal (DL-8342): the customer purchased through AWS Marketplace but CloudResell will be acting as the reseller and wants to issue the customer invoice. We need to confirm two things before we finalize onboarding:

1) Tax withholding: will AWS or CloudResell withhold any tax at source when remitting to Redwood? If CloudResell collects in-region (EU) and issues the customer invoice, do we need to expect any withholding or VAT margin scheme implications? Also curious about LATAM withholding if the customer later uses a local billing method.

2) Pass-through invoice / supplier docs: CloudResell says they require a Redwood VAT registration or supplier invoice to produce a pass-through invoice. Do we submit our VAT number to AWS partner console, or directly to the reseller? What forms do we need pre-populated (W-8/W-9 for US entity, W-8BEN-E if applicable)?

Attaching the PO (po_2048.pdf) and a rough supplier packet we use internally. Rafael / Marissa looping you for finance/legal visibility — any internal must-haves before we share docs with the reseller?

Thanks,
Vanessa
Account Lead, Cloud Partnerships
Redwood Inference

From: Sara Khan <sara.khan@amazon.com>

Subject: Re: Reseller withholding / pass-through invoice process for marketplace co-sell

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the note and congrats on the co-sell. Short answers: it depends on the listing model and the reseller arrangement. In AWS terminology there are a few flows:

- "AWS as transacting party" (typical public marketplace SaaS listings): AWS bills the customer and remits net to you; AWS issues marketplace invoices to the customer and manages VAT collection for the transaction where required. In that flow you usually do not see customer invoices directly.

- "Reseller/Channel" flow (where partner seats and collects payment): the partner (CloudResell) is the transacting party in the region they operate. They may issue the customer invoice and then remit to you. In that case, tax treatment is between the partner and their customer.

For Redwood to avoid immediate withholding surprises:

- US tax: If Redwood is a US entity receiving payments from an entity in the US (or reporting required by a US payer), AWS may request a W-9, and non-US entities provide W-8BEN-E. If CloudResell is collecting and remitting from their EU entity, US withholding typically isn’t triggered, but that depends on where the payment is booked.

- EU VAT: If the partner issues the customer invoice in the EU, they will likely charge VAT unless they are doing a margin scheme or are zero-rating under a reverse-charge. CloudResell should confirm their VAT treatment. You should provide your VAT registration number if they need to produce a supplier invoice to pass-through costs.

Action items I recommend:
1) CloudResell: confirm which legal entity will be the billing entity for the customer (EU entity name + VAT ID).
2) Redwood: upload supplier tax docs (W-8/W-9 and VAT reg) to the AWS Partner Network / Marketplace seller console OR share directly with partner if they need a copy for invoicing.
3) Finance: agree on a monthly reconciliation: partner issues invoice to customer; partner invoices Redwood (net) monthly with backing docs; Redwood issues invoice to partner or accepts partner remittance depending on negotiated terms.

Useful doc: https://aws.amazon.com/marketplace/help/Marketplace-Billing

Happy to jump on a 15-min call if you want to walk through the exact attachment points in the console.

—Sara
AWS Marketplace Partner Mgmt

From: Luis Romero <luis.romero@cloudresell.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Sara Khan <sara.khan@amazon.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 08:03:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Reseller withholding / pass-through invoice process for marketplace co-sell

Vanessa / Sara,

Thanks — CloudResell will be the billing entity for the EU customer and we will issue the customer invoice. A couple clarifications from our side:

- We need Redwood to provide a supplier invoice (monthly) with Redwood's VAT number so we can include it as a pass-through line item when we bill the customer. Without your VAT ID we will need to charge VAT on our margin and on the product, which creates friction for the customer.

- LATAM: for Brazil/Mexico customers we sometimes see withholding. We'll flag country-specific withholding on our invoice to Redwood if it occurs; those withholdings are typically tax credits we reconcile in the monthly settlement. If Redwood prefers to avoid exposure, we can propose a gross-up clause in the channel contract (we'll need legal to sign off).

Please tell us which Redwood entity to invoice and send the appropriate tax docs to contracts@cloudresell.com.

—Luis
Director, Finance Operations
CloudResell Inc.

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Reseller withholding / pass-through invoice process for marketplace co-sell

Vanessa — internal note on next steps from finance/legal perspective:

1) Documents to collect BEFORE going live: completed W-8BEN-E (if non-US entity) OR W-9 (if we end up transacting with a US payer), Redwood VAT registration certificate (EU tax ID), and a copy of CloudResell's reseller agreement showing which entity is billing.

2) Invoicing workflow we prefer: CloudResell issues customer invoice -> CloudResell invoices Redwood monthly (line-itemed with VAT and country withholding noted) -> Redwood pays net amount on agreed payment terms. This preserves a clean audit trail.

3) Withholdings / Credits: when CloudResell reports withholding in LATAM we will accept a withholding tax certificate from CloudResell to claim foreign tax credits; include the withholding certificate and the customer invoice in the monthly packet.

4) Contract recommendation: add a clause requiring partner to notify Redwood of any tax collected at source within 7 business days of collection and to provide supporting docs (withholding certificates, VAT receipts). Also include an indemnity limited to taxes not reasonably foreseeable. Legal will draft a short addendum.

I attached our recommended supplier packet for partners (draft_supplier_packet.docx). Vanessa, please confirm which Redwood legal entity: Redwood Inference, Inc. (US, EIN 12-3456789) or Redwood EU Ltd (EU VAT GB123456789) should appear on invoices to CloudResell. If they will bill us via an EU entity, provide the EU billing entity details.

—Rafael
Head of Finance 
Redwood Inference

Attachments: draft_supplier_packet.docx
